intention: 进入壁垒（阻止新竞争者进入市场的障碍）
pattern: Barriers to entry include well-recognised brands.
sentencePatterns: High barriers to entry make it difficult for new players to compete.
realLifeExamples: Barriers to entry in the pharma industry include patents and high R&D costs.
usageNotes: Business term. Always plural: 'barriers to entry'. Common barriers: brand, capital, regulation, distribution.

intention: 评估并分析（商业写作标配组合）
pattern: assess and analyse the competitive forces
sentencePatterns: We need to assess and analyse...
This report aims to assess and analyse the risks before...
realLifeExamples: We need to assess and analyse the risks before launching the product.
usageNotes: assess = judge value/degree; analyse = break structure down. These two are often paired in formal writing.

intention: 进而会……（链式因果中间连接）
pattern: ..., which, in turn, would lower your profitability.
sentencePatterns: ..., which, in turn, would lower profitability.
..., which, in turn, would increase costs significantly.
realLifeExamples: Higher raw material prices, which, in turn, would reduce our profit margins.
usageNotes: 'in turn' inserted as adverb phrase between 'which' and the verb. Signals a chain reaction: A causes B, which in turn causes C.

id: in terms of time or money
pattern: It costs little in terms of time or money to...
sentencePatterns: If it costs little in terms of time or money to...
We need to evaluate this in terms of time or money.
realLifeExamples: In terms of time or money, this approach is far more efficient.
usageNotes: 'in terms of' specifies the dimension. Can extend: in terms of quality, risk, efficiency, cost, etc.

pattern: It is easy for competitors to take market share away from you.
sentencePatterns: Competitors can take market share away from you if...
We need to prevent rivals from taking market share away from us.
realLifeExamples: Cheaper alternatives took significant market share away from the brand.
usageNotes: 'take sth away from sb' = remove from someone's possession. Market share is uncountable here.

intention: 在价格上胜过对手，取得价格优势
pattern: Reduce costs to gain a price advantage over competitors.
sentencePatterns: ...to gain a price advantage over your competitors.
If we cut costs, we can gain a price advantage over rivals.
realLifeExamples: The company adopted automation to gain a price advantage over its competitors.
usageNotes: 'gain an advantage over' is fixed. Extends to: competitive / cost / technological advantage over sb.

pattern: The brand can charge a premium price for its products.
sentencePatterns: ...allows companies to charge a premium price for it.
A strong brand lets you charge a premium price for your service.
realLifeExamples: Apple charges a premium price for its products because of strong brand loyalty.
usageNotes: 'charge a price for sth' is the structure. premium = above-average price reflecting perceived extra value.

id: concentrate on a narrow segment of the market
intention: 聚焦于细分市场的某一小领域
pattern: concentrate on a narrow segment of the market and satisfy unique needs
sentencePatterns: ...concentrate on a narrow segment of the market.
By concentrating on a narrow segment, a company can enjoy high customer loyalty.
realLifeExamples: Our startup concentrates on a narrow segment of the market: enterprise security tools for SMBs.
usageNotes: 'segment of the market' = distinct customer subgroup. 'narrow' emphasises focused scope of the focus strategy.
